data.one_liner: Multi-purpose immutable DateTime subclass with support for multiple localizations and human-readable formats
data.what_it_does: Provides an immutable subclass of DateTime inspired by moment.js for converting DateTimes and Durations into human-readable relative formats, handling localizations, and providing various helper methods for date manipulation.
use_when: You need to display relative time strings like 'a day ago' or 'in 5 seconds'.
Your app requires robust multi-language localization support for dates and durations.
You want immutable DateTime instances with convenience methods for week, year, and range operations.
avoid_when: You only need basic, unlocalized Dart core DateTime manipulation without any formatting overhead.
strengths: Supports multiple localizations out of the box.
Implements precise and relative duration formatting.
Provides numerous helper methods and extension-like features on DateTime and Duration.
weaknesses: Adds an external dependency on a custom DateTime subclass instead of using core types directly.
data.minimal_example:
final yesterday = Moment.now() - const Duration(days: 1);
yesterday.fromNow(); // a day ago
